answer: A good proof of work is quieter than it looks: a whisper of effort repeated until it becomes a habit, and the habit, held long enough, becomes something durable. I think of learning as polishing an opal — the surface stays plain until the light catches it from the right angle, and then the colour was already there, waiting. The zenith of a craft is not a loud summit but the moment the work starts to speak for itself, plainly and without ornament. That is the standard I hold myself to: small, steady, verifiable steps, and work that can be checked by anyone, at any time.
